newsitem.title: USA: USDA AUG 12 WORLD GRAIN HIGHLIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: USDA AUG 12 WORLD GRAIN HIGHLIGHTS.

text.p: World grain production will total 1,851.18 million tonnes in 1997/98, down from 1,864.38 million tonnes estimated last month, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday.
World output would include 596.39 million tonnes of wheat, 875.52 million of coarse (feed) grains and 379.27 million of rice. Oilseeds were pegged at 275.03 million tonnes.
USDA pegged Brazil's 1997/98 soybean crop at 28.00 million tonnes, unchanged from its estimate last month. It left the 1997/98 Argentine soybean harvest at 13.90 million.
Soybean exports in 1997/98 from Brazil and Argentina were estimated at 7.25 million tonnes and 1.50 million, respectively.
USDA forecast Brazil 1997/98 soybean imports at 2.25 million tonnes, up sharply from 800,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
The department said U.S. 1997/98 soybean crush and export prospects were increased based on stronger import demand in China for soybeans and products.
China's imports during 1997/98 were estimated at 1.60 million tonnes of soyoil, 3.35 million of soymeal and 2.70 million of soybeans.
China corn exports were cut in half to 1.00 million tonnes and production was cut 12 million tonnes to 110 million tonnes due to drought conditions.

U.S. wheat imports, which virtually all come from Canada, were forecast at 2.59 million tonnes, down from 2.72 million tonnes forecast in July, but up slightly from 2.51 million in 1996/97. The rising imports are a source of trade friction.
The USDA lowered wheat crop and export forecasts for Australia, Canada and Argentina due to unfavorable weather conditions. It raised its forecast for the China wheat crop by 7.00 million tonnes.
